notes: Claude Haiku 5.5 launch headline table, parsed from the fetched HTML <table> (BenchmarkGrid) in code and diffed cell by cell against scores[]. Columns: Haiku 5.5, Haiku 4.5, GPT-6 Luna, and Sonnet 5.5 marked "For reference". The table has no footnote markers; the only effort label is Sonnet 5.5 FrontierCode "Xhigh". All other efforts are `unknown` here, with the system-card or chart corroboration named in each caveat. Haiku 4.5 rows carry effort null (no effort parameter). OSWorld 2.1 is the offline subset (82 tasks) partial-credit score and has its own comparability_group. Dash cells are listed in missing[]. Metric IDs reuse catalog definitions.

claims.statement: Anthropic says Haiku 5.5 costs around 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5 on average. Footnote 2: it is priced 90% lower for requests up to 100,000 tokens and 50% lower above; 90% of Haiku 4.5 requests were up to 100,000 tokens; the calculation accounts for the updated tokenizer, which uses slightly more tokens per task.
claims.implication: Vendor average with an unpublished workload mix; not reproducible from list prices. List-price ratio is 0.10 below 100K and 0.50 above. Weighting the tiers 90/10 (the request split, treated as the spend split) gives 0.14 (86% less) before tokenizer effects; with the docs' approximately 30% more tokens for the same text it gives about 0.18 (82% less). Reaching 0.25 (75% less) at 1.3x tokens needs requests over 100K to carry about 23% of Haiku 4.5 spend, or more output/thinking tokens per task. The 1.3x token growth also pushes Haiku 4.5 prompts of roughly 77K-100K tokens over the 100K threshold. The launch post says the tokenizer uses "slightly more tokens per task"; the docs say "approximately 30% more tokens" for the same text. The launch SVG costs show the saving depends on effort: at medium Haiku 5.5 costs less per task than Haiku 4.5 on all four charts, but at max it costs more on GDPval-AA ($0.87 vs $0.24), HLE no tools ($0.21 vs $0.09) and Terminal-Bench 4.0 ($2.64 vs $0.79).

claims.statement: Starting 2026-10-07 Sonnet 5.5 cache reads cost $0.10 per million tokens instead of $0.20; Anthropic says this makes Sonnet 5.5 around 20% cheaper on most agentic work.
claims.implication: Vendor claim. The launch Terminal-Bench 4.0 chart shows the per-task cost of each Sonnet 5.5 effort falling 21-26% (e.g. max $14.15 -> $10.44) with unchanged scores.

claims.statement: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 remain better choices for complex agentic coding tasks like Terminal-Bench 4.0, and Haiku 5.5 is best suited to narrowly scoped tasks such as compaction, summarization, or subagent work.
claims.implication: On the launch Terminal-Bench 4.0 chart, Sonnet 5.5 at high (43.0%, $1.46 at $0.10 cache reads) beats Haiku 5.5 at max (39.2%, $2.64).

claims.statement: Anthropic calls Haiku 5.5 its fastest model to date at each model's standard speed; footnote 1 says it runs less quickly than Opus models in Fast Mode.
claims.implication: No latency numbers are published on the launch page; customer quotes (Asana, Box) give relative latency only.
